modules.name: ShortenService
modules.responsibility: Accepts a long URL, validates it, generates a unique short code, and persists the mapping. Owns the encoding strategy and collision handling.

modules.name: RedirectService
modules.responsibility: Resolves a short code to its target URL and issues an HTTP 301/302 redirect. Emits a click event asynchronously without blocking the redirect.
interfaces:
class Redirector(Protocol):
    def redirect(self, code: str) -> RedirectResult: ...

modules.name: StatsService
modules.responsibility: Records click events and aggregates them into per-link statistics (total clicks, time-bucketed counts, referrer/UA breakdown).

modules.name: RateLimiter
modules.responsibility: Enforces per-client request quotas across shorten and redirect endpoints using a token-bucket/fixed-window policy keyed by client identity.
interfaces:
class RateLimiter(Protocol):
    def check(self, key: str, *, cost: int = 1) -> RateDecision: ...

modules.name: ApiGateway
modules.responsibility: HTTP entrypoint. Routes requests, applies rate limiting, maps domain results/errors to HTTP responses, and wires dependencies.
interfaces:
class Endpoint(Protocol):
    def handle(self, request: Request) -> Response: ...
injection_points: All services via constructor injection / DI container

data_model.name: ClickEvent

fields.name: ip_hash
fields.note: SHA-256(ip + daily salt), never raw IP

relationships: many ClickEvent belong to one ShortLink

fields.name: key
fields.note: client identity (api key hash or ip hash)

ux_flows.name: Shorten a URL
steps: Gateway applies rate limit check on client key
ShortenService validates URL scheme/host and length
CodeGenerator produces unique code (retry on collision)
ux_flows.success_criteria: Returns a resolvable short URL in a single request with HTTP 201
i18n_considerations: Error messages localized via message catalog
Support IDN/punycode hosts in input URLs

ux_flows.name: Redirect
ux_flows.success_criteria: Median redirect latency under 50ms; click recorded without blocking

ux_flows.name: View click stats
ux_flows.success_criteria: Owner retrieves accurate aggregate stats in one request
i18n_considerations: Date bucket labels formatted per locale/timezone

customer_journey: A developer integrating the service discovers it via API docs. They POST a long URL and immediately receive a short link they can share — no signup required for anonymous use, an API key unlocks higher rate limits and stats access. Their audience clicks the short link and is redirected near-instantly to the destination, while each click is silently recorded. Later the developer queries the stats endpoint to see total clicks, daily trends, and top referrers for their link, using this to measure campaign reach. Throughout, abusive traffic is throttled by rate limiting so the service stays fast and available for legitimate users.

experience_metric.metric: Shorten and receive a working redirect URL in 1 API call
experience_metric.target: p95 shorten latency ≤ 150ms; p95 redirect latency ≤ 50ms; 0 extra round-trips
experience_metric.measurement: Latency histograms per endpoint plus call-count per shorten operation

architecture_decisions.title: Short code generation strategy
architecture_decisions.context: Codes must be globally unique, short, hard to enumerate trivially, and cheap to generate at high throughput. Options: (a) sequential ID encoded as base62, (b) random base62 with collision-check, (c) hash of URL truncated.
architecture_decisions.decision: Use random 7-character base62 codes (~3.5T space) with a unique constraint and bounded retry on collision; allow optional user-supplied custom aliases.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Random codes avoid leaking creation order/volume (an enumeration and business-intelligence risk of sequential IDs) and decouple code generation from a central counter, easing horizontal scaling. 7 chars of base62 keeps URLs short while collision probability stays negligible until billions of links, where retry handles the rare clash.
consequences: Requires a unique index and insert-retry loop on the store
Codes are not sortable by creation time (use created_at instead)
Custom aliases need a separate reserved-word/profanity check
Slightly higher write cost than pure sequential under extreme collision rates

architecture_decisions.title: Asynchronous click recording on the redirect path
architecture_decisions.context: Redirects are latency-critical and far more frequent than shortens. Writing a click record synchronously couples redirect availability/latency to the stats store.
architecture_decisions.decision: Emit ClickEvents through a non-blocking ClickRecorder (in-process queue/buffer, pluggable to a real broker) so the redirect responds before the click is durably stored.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Single-responsibility and resilience: a slow or down stats store must never degrade redirects. Decoupling lets stats scale independently and be eventually consistent, which is acceptable for analytics.
consequences: Stats are eventually consistent; brief loss possible on crash without a durable queue
Need backpressure handling when the buffer fills
Adds a queue dependency as an injection point

threat_model.description: Open redirect / malicious destinations — attacker shortens links pointing to phishing or malware, abusing the service's trusted domain reputation.
threat_model.mitigation: Validate URL scheme (http/https only), block internal/loopback/metadata hosts (SSRF/redirect guard), optional safe-browsing reputation check, and allow takedown/blocklisting by code.

threat_model.description: Flood of shorten or redirect requests exhausts storage and compute, degrading service for all clients.
threat_model.mitigation: Token-bucket rate limiting per client key and IP hash, with stricter anonymous quotas and a global circuit breaker; rate-limit applied before expensive work.

threat_model.description: Enumeration of short codes or stats endpoints exposes others' destination URLs and click analytics (which may reveal PII patterns).
threat_model.mitigation: Random non-sequential codes; stats endpoint requires owner API key authorization; store IP only as salted hash; no listing endpoint.

privacy_inventory.purpose: Abuse prevention and unique-visitor estimation for stats
privacy_inventory.retention: Never stored raw; only salted SHA-256 hash retained 90 days
privacy_inventory.encryption: Hashed at ingestion (daily-rotating salt); store encrypted at rest
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Hash rotation makes re-identification infeasible after salt rotation; per-link delete cascades ClickEvents
Deleted on link deletion and on retention expiry job

privacy_inventory.retention: Lifetime of link or until expires_at

i18n_plan.rtl_strategy: Logical CSS properties and dir=auto on branded error/landing pages; API responses locale-agnostic except localized error messages selected by Accept-Language
i18n_plan.notes: Accept and normalize IDN/punycode hostnames; format stat dates/numbers per request locale and timezone

open_questions: Persistence backend for v1: single SQL store vs. KV (Redis) for links + columnar store for clicks?
Is anonymous (keyless) shortening allowed, or is an API key mandatory? Affects rate-limit keying and stats ownership.
Default link expiration policy — never expire, or TTL with renewal?
Is a durable message broker in scope for iteration 2, or is in-process buffering acceptable (accepting click-loss on crash)?
Required throughput/scale targets to size rate-limit store (in-memory vs distributed)?

sections.title: Digest
sections.content: url-shortener (iter 2): five modules — ShortenService, RedirectService, StatsService, RateLimiter, ApiGateway — wired via Protocol interfaces and constructor DI. Core flows: POST /shorten -> random 7-char base62 code (ADR-001); GET /{code} -> 302 redirect with async click recording (ADR-002); GET /stats/{code} -> owner-authorized aggregates. Data: ShortLink, ClickEvent (PII-derived: IP stored only as salted hash, 90d retention), LinkStats, RateLimitBucket. Experience metric: shorten+resolvable link in 1 call, p95 redirect ≤50ms. Top threats: open-redirect/SSRF, DoS (rate limiting), code-enumeration/info-disclosure. Privacy: no raw IPs, cascade erasure on link delete. Open: storage backend, keyless vs key-required, expiry policy, durable queue scope.

sections.title: Module Boundaries
sections.content: ShortenService (encode/validate/persist), RedirectService (resolve+emit click), StatsService (record+aggregate), RateLimiter (token bucket per client key), ApiGateway (routing, limit enforcement, error mapping). All collaboration via Protocols; storage and clock injected.

sections.title: Key Decisions
sections.content: ADR-001 random base62 codes with collision retry over sequential IDs to prevent enumeration and ease scaling. ADR-002 async click recording so analytics store never blocks redirect latency/availability.
